articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA, the agency that's supposed to protect us from cyber threats, left AWS GovCloud credentials sitting on GitHub like a drunk teenager posting their diary online. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a compromised private key.

articles.title: CISA Exposes Secrets, Credentials in 'Private' Repo
articles.summary: YellowKey, GreenPlasma, and MiniPlasma continue the Windows zero-day parade that's making Patch Tuesday look more like Patch Decade. Microsoft's playing whack-a-mole with vulnerabilities and losing badly.

articles.title: Your Privacy Shouldn't Be A Corporate Decision
articles.summary: Microsoft actually took a step toward human rights accountability in their tech deals with authoritarian governments. Hell has officially frozen over, and we're here for this rare moment of corporate conscience.

articles.title: We Updated Our Privacy Policy. Here's What Changed and Why.
articles.summary: Meta's internal docs reveal they planned to launch facial recognition during political chaos when civil rights groups would be 'distracted.' Classic surveillance capitalism: exploit democracy's busy schedule to spy on everyone.

articles.title: The New Phishing Click: How OAuth Consent Bypasses MFA
articles.summary: DirtyDecrypt PoC drops for Linux kernel CVE-2026-31635, because apparently we needed another privilege escalation exploit with a catchy name. The kernel vulnerability industrial complex keeps churning out the hits.

articles.title: TeamPCP Supply Chain Campaign: Activity Through 2026-05-17, (Mon, May 18th)
articles.summary: MiniPlasma zero-day gives SYSTEM access on fully patched Windows 11 systems, proving once again that 'fully patched' is Microsoft's idea of a cruel joke. PoC included for your educational panic attacks.

articles.title: Trapdoor Android Ad Fraud Scheme Hit 659 Million Daily Bid Requests Using 455 Apps
articles.summary: TeamPCP claims to have breached GitHub's internal repositories and is selling the source code like it's a yard sale. The platform where we store all our secrets got its own secrets stolen—poetry in motion.

articles.title: Grafana says hackers hit its GitHub environment, demand ransom to prevent codebase release — but it's refusing to pay
articles.summary: Hackers stole Grafana's open-source code and demanded ransom to not release it publicly, which is like stealing a library book and threatening to read it out loud. Grafana rightfully told them to pound sand.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: Scattered Spider member 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after SMS phishing campaigns that actually worked. Another young hacker trades their keyboard for an orange jumpsuit—tale as old as time.

articles.title: Mexican government breached by solo user with Claude, 150 GB exfiltrated
articles.summary: 7-Eleven confirms data breach after ShinyHunters threatens to leak 600,000 Salesforce records including personal and corporate data. Your Slurpee loyalty points were never worth this level of digital drama.
